newsitem.title: USA: GE's NBC tops Nov. sweeps ratings - Nielsen.
newsitem.headline: GE's NBC tops Nov. sweeps ratings - Nielsen.

text.p: Nielsen Media Research said Monday General Electric Corp's NBC unit maintained its lead over Westinghouse Electric Co's CBS and Walt Disney Co's ABC during the critical November "sweeps" period.

NBC attracted the largest average evening-hours audience, earning an 11.3 rating, or percentage, of America's 97 million television-viewing households, and an 18 percent share of televion sets in use during those hours, Nielsen said.
CBS and ABC were tied with a 10.2 rating and a 17 percent share, according to the market researcher.
The November month covers the period of October 31 to November 27.

In a conference call held prior to the release of the latest Nielsen data, CBS Entertainment President Leslie Moonves said that while CBS remains in second place, the latest figures mark a four percent year-on-year growth in ratings.
"We are the only one of the 'big three' that is up from a year ago in November," Moonves said, noting that NBC's ratings are down 5 percent, while ABC's ratings slipped by 10 percent.
"We all feel that we have stopped the bleeding, and have gotten on the road to recovery," he added.
The CBS executive said the network's focus on its older core audience and its use of established artists are the source its gains.
"I think big stars have helped get us back in the ball game," he said, noting that new shows starring the likes of Bill Cosby and Ted Danson have been succesful this year.
